summary: This resolution directs the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities against Iran, except those needed to defend against imminent attack, unless Congress passes a declaration of war or specific authorization.

scores.thoughts: The resolution directs removal of U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran. While ending military operations can produce modest savings, the text contains no appropriations language, budget directives, or explicit spending changes; any fiscal effect is indirect and secondary to the war-powers question.
No provisions address tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue measures of any kind.
The bill is silent on health-care policy, coverage, or markets.
No reference to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No immigration, border, or visa provisions appear in the text.
The resolution does not address reproductive health or abortion access.

The core purpose is to direct the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities against Iran (with narrow self-defense exceptions). This directly limits ongoing military engagement and therefore pushes toward lower defense outlays for that operation.
No environmental, regulatory, or climate-related content.
The bill contains no welfare, entitlement, or social-services provisions.
No education funding, policy, or school-choice language.
No drug-enforcement or decriminalization measures.
The resolution does not address sentencing, policing, or criminal-justice reform.
No trade, tariff, or globalization provisions.
Any reduction in hostilities could marginally slow deficit growth, but the text never references debt, deficits, or fiscal targets; the connection is too attenuated to score.
No LGBTQ-related legal protections or limitations are mentioned.
The measure concerns combat operations, not foreign-assistance funding or programs.
No voting-access, election-integrity, or campaign provisions.
The bill is silent on technology regulation or data privacy.
No labor, union, or worker-protection content.
No religious-exemption or civil-rights provisions appear.
